source.title: Demystifying Batch Normalization in ReLU Networks: Equivalent Convex Optimization Models and Implicit Regularization
source.authors: Tolga Ergen; Arda Sahiner; Batu Mehmet Ozturkler; J. Pauly; Morteza Mardani; Mert Pilanci

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendix, is present. No apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extracting the relevant results.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 training-accuracy results for BN networks and related convex formulations, bearing on whether the reported recipes reach near-100% training accuracy. It does not test the claim's random-initialization, corrupted-label, depth-shortcut, or other initialization scenarios.
record.gate_note: Rows capture the paper's reported CIFAR training-accuracy outcomes for the baseline BN model and its truncated, convex, and convex-truncated comparators. The authors state that the longer-run models can near 100% training accuracy; exact values are shown only in figures. The paper also reports CIFAR-10 CNN training accuracy in Table 1. Theoretical optimality claims and cited prior work are not empirical training-result rows.
record.test_reason: The two-layer CIFAR-10 CNN experiments bear on V1's allowance for substantial training error under finite, regularized training. Appendix A.7.5 also compares accuracy over training time with and without BN, bearing on V6 in a fully connected CIFAR setting. The near-perfect fitting results in Figure 7 concern fully connected networks, outside V1's convolutional scope.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the extended-training observation, but understates the paper's main conclusion. The authors derive equivalent convex representations and some closed-form optimal solutions for regularized BN ReLU networks. They show that GD on the original parametrization preferentially learns high-singular-value directions, and propose truncation to reproduce this regularization in whitened formulations. Longer fully connected CIFAR training increases fitting and overfitting without improving test performance.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains two-layer ReLU networks with BN and weight decay using SGD, Adam, or AdamW, but experiments are not a direct reproduction of the claim's random-label or plain-network conditions; includes convex and singular-value-truncated formulations.
record.method_sensitivity: Training duration, dataset, model/formulation, optimizer, learning rate, batch size, and singular-value truncation affect the reported accuracy curves or performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Extended training brings the fully connected CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 models and their formulations near 100% training accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Two-layer fully connected BN ReLU models and the compared formulations can nearly interpolate clean CIFAR training labels with longer training.

fits_no_version.finding: The convex CNN relaxations attain 81.60% and 81.35% training accuracy after 50 epochs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed convex CNN relaxations achieve similar test performance while retaining substantial training error in this experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: GD remains above the closed-form optimum after 40001 epochs in the three-class, 1500-example CIFAR experiment.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: GD need not attain the global regularized squared-loss optimum of these fully connected BN networks. This does not establish classification error or V2's teacher-student local-minimum frequency.

record.problems: CIFAR main accuracy curves are figures without exact train-accuracy values in the text. Table 1 provides exact train accuracy for a separate CIFAR-10 CNN setup but only 50 epochs. The paper reports no uncertainty estimates for these outcomes. Training accuracy is reported in figures as accuracy rather than classification error.
record.rows_left_out: No reported results meeting the row criteria were omitted. Figure 3 and Figure 7 test-accuracy curves were left out because they do not measure training classification error/accuracy; training-accuracy Figure 7 curves are retained as figure-only rows.

untested.parts: Near-zero training error in sufficiently large CNNs after sufficient training; corrupted or random labels; CIFAR-100 CNN fitting; width comparisons; and a controlled training-duration comparison for CNNs.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, frequencies of spurious local minima, and adding one or two student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth, identity-shortcut controls, very deep tanh networks, and Fixup.
Comparative initialization effects on speed or trainable depth. Using Kaiming initialization alone does not test these effects.
Learning rates relative to an initial stability threshold, curvature trajectories, catapult recovery, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence.
A controlled maximum-stable-learning-rate comparison, the named original architectures and datasets, and the Fixup alternative. Selected learning rates alone do not establish learning-rate tolerance.

missing.what: BN versus no-BN accuracy-over-time comparisons for the standard non-convex two-layer networks on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100. Record paired conditions and readable curve values; distinguish these from convex-method comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text contains figure captions and axes but does not preserve readable curve trajectories. Exact Figure 7 endpoints and a Figure 13 speedup cannot be recovered. No verdict is based on the cited prior studies or on existence of an optimal solution alone.

versions.untested_parts: The CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 experiments report training accuracy for BN models and variants, but do not report random or corrupted labels, Adam for the main CIFAR accuracy sweeps is only in supplementary tests, or comparisons with smaller models and early stopping as described by the version.
